production.format_and_medium.summary: A public agency shall provide an electronic copy or a paper copy of a public record at the option of the person making the request.

production.no_duty_to_create_or_convert.summary: An agency is not required to reprogram a computer system to provide enhanced access or access to a governmental entity by an electronic device.

eligibility.any_person.summary: Any person may inspect and copy the public records of any public agency during the agency's regular business hours.

eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.summary: A public agency may not deny a request because the requester refuses to state the purpose of the request, unless another applicable statute requires it.

eligibility.no_residency_requirement.summary: The right to inspect and copy public records extends to any person; the Act imposes no residency or citizenship qualification.

dup.bw.rate.label: Copy rate — B&W page
dup.bw.rate.unit: USD per page (non-color), or the agency's actual cost of copying if greater (actual cost = paper + per-page equipment cost only; no labor or overhead)
dup.bw.rate.notes: Local regime: the fiscal body (city/town council) 'shall establish a fee schedule' by ordinance; the schedule may not exceed the greater of $0.10/page (non-color) or actual cost as narrowly defined. PAC opinions (19-FC-67, 21-FC-1, 22-FC-145) treat $0.10 as the practical cap for standard-size B&W…

dup.color.rate.label: Copy rate — color page
dup.color.rate.unit: USD per page (color), or the agency's actual cost of copying if greater (paper + per-page equipment cost only)
dup.color.rate.notes: Same clause as dup.bw.rate; color ceiling $0.25/page. Fiscal body sets the operative rate under the ceiling; must be uniform throughout the agency and to all purchasers.

dup.oversized.rate.label: Copy rate — oversized / nonstandard page
dup.oversized.rate.value: actual cost to the agency of copying the document (cost of paper and the per-page cost for use of copying or facsimile equipment; excludes labor and overhead)
dup.oversized.rate.notes: No separate oversized/nonstandard rate for local agencies; § 8(d) lets the fee reach 'the actual cost to the agency of copying the document' when that exceeds $0.10/$0.25, and the PAC reads that branch as the one for 'unusually sized pieces of paper' (19-FC-67, quoted). Statutory 'actual cost' de…

dup.specialty.rate.label: Specialty reproduction (photos, maps, transcripts)
dup.specialty.rate.value: electronic maps: 'reasonable percentage of the agency's direct cost of maintaining, upgrading, and enhancing the electronic map' plus 'the direct cost of supplying the electronic map in the form requested', subject to fiscal-body approval; other specialty duplicates (photos, transcripts, microfilm): § 8(g) 'direct cost of supplying the information in that form' or § 8(d) actual cost
dup.specialty.rate.authority: Ind. Code § 5-14-3-8(j) (electronic map); § 5-14-3-8(g) (duplicates of microfilm/electronic media); § 5-14-3-8(d)
dup.specialty.rate.notes: No statutory dollar figure for photos, maps or transcripts. Electronic map fee is a soft standard with a structural gate (fiscal-body approval) and a noncommercial waiver (§ 8(k), IN-9011). PAC 25-FC-145 (2025) upheld a $750 commercial GIS fee computed under a county ordinance.

dup.tiers.label: Graduated page bands (per-page rate by volume)
dup.tiers.notes: No graduated per-page bands anywhere in APRA. § 8(d) requires a fee schedule 'uniform throughout the public agency and uniform to all purchasers' — a single ceiling per page type, not volume tiers. Searched: Ind. Code 5-14-3 (APRA) §§ 3, 3.3, 3.5, 6, 8, 8.1, 8.3, 8.5, 9 as reproduced in the PAC H…

rules.freePages.label: Free page allowance per request
rules.freePages.notes: No free-page allowance in statute for local agencies. Only categorical free items: inspection (§ 8(b)(1)) and electronic copies sent by e-mail (§ 8(b)(4), IN-9002). Some state offices publish courtesy allowances (e.g., Treasurer of State guide: e-mail up to five pages free) — agency practice, not…

labor.search.rate.label: Labor rate — search / retrieval ($/hr)
labor.search.rate.notes: Search/retrieval labor is categorically non-chargeable for ordinary requests, so no rate exists to configure. Exceptions that DO carry staff-time money: (i) HEA 1360 § 8(n) supplemental fee for non-Indiana residents/out-of-state entities — ceiling $25 per hour of staff time (IN-9007, eff. July 1,…

labor.review.rate.label: Labor rate — review / redaction ($/hr)
labor.review.rate.notes: No fee 'to search for, examine, or review a record to determine whether the record may be disclosed' — review/redaction labor is not chargeable. PAC 25-FC-121 (Feb. 17, 2026): where redaction of a body-camera recording requires making a copy, the § 8(g) copy fee (≤ $150) applies, but no separate …

labor.programming.rate.label: Labor rate — programming / data extraction ($/hr)
labor.programming.rate.value: direct cost of reprogramming a computer system — 'direct cost' = 105% of the sum of (1) initial program development, if any, (2) labor required to retrieve electronically stored data, and (3) any medium used for electronic output
labor.programming.rate.notes: No hourly rate; the standard is the statutorily defined 'direct cost' (with a fixed 105% multiplier — see labor.overheadPct). Chargeable only when reprogramming is required to separate disclosable from nondisclosable electronically stored information; agencies are not required to reprogram to pro…

labor.billableWhen.label: When labor is chargeable at all (never / always / only over N pages or N hours; paper-only scope)
labor.billableWhen.value: never for ordinary requests — no fee to inspect or to search/examine/review (§ 8(b)(1),(3)), and paper 'actual cost' expressly excludes labor and overhead (§ 8(d)); labor enters only via (a) 'direct cost' for electronic duplicates/reprogramming (§ 8(g), § 6(c)); (b) HEA 1360 § 8(n) supplemental fee for non-Indiana requesters (≤ $25/hr staff time, eff. 7/1/2026); (c) school corporations only, electronic search > 5 hours (§ 8(m))
labor.billableWhen.notes: Statute-set (not city-set): the city cannot make labor chargeable for standard paper/electronic requests. PAC 19-FC-67 and 19-FC-90 struck local ordinances that folded labor/overhead into copy fees.

labor.overheadPct.label: Overhead / fringe surcharge on labor (%)
labor.overheadPct.unit: % (the 'direct cost' formula is 105% of program-development + retrieval-labor + medium costs) — applies ONLY to § 8(g) electronic duplicates and § 6(c) reprogramming; for paper copies § 8(d) 'actual cost' expressly excludes labor and overhead
labor.overheadPct.notes: The 105% multiplier is the only overhead-type figure in Indiana public-records fee law. Not a general fringe/overhead surcharge on labor — labor itself is non-chargeable outside the direct-cost contexts. Also note (g)(1) caps law-enforcement-recording copies at $150 regardless of direct cost.

labor.increment.label: Labor time increment + rounding
labor.increment.notes: No time-increment/rounding rule for municipalities (labor is not chargeable). The only increment language is school-only § 8(m): 'The fee must be prorated to reflect any search time of less than one (1) hour' and 'may charge only for time that the person making the search actually spends'; § 8(n)…

rules.freeLaborHours.label: Free labor hours per request
rules.freeLaborHours.authority: Ind. Code § 5-14-3-8(b)(3); cf. § 8(m) (schools: first 5 hours free)
rules.freeLaborHours.notes: Moot for municipalities: search/review labor is never chargeable, so there is no 'free hours before billing' threshold. The five-free-hours rule exists only for school corporations and charter schools (§ 8(m), IN-9015). Not a municipal parameter.

rules.deposit.threshold.label: Deposit / prepayment may be required above ($)
rules.deposit.threshold.value: no statutory threshold — a public agency 'may require that the payment for search and copying costs be made in advance' for any amount; the city decides whether and when to invoke prepayment
rules.deposit.threshold.notes: Advance payment is a Permission with no dollar trigger; not a 'deposit' concept — full payment of search and copying costs may be required before copies are made (25-FC-121 upheld advance payment of a $150 body-cam copy fee). Inspection can never be conditioned on a fee (§ 8(b)(1)).

rules.deposit.percent.label: Deposit capped at (% of estimate)
rules.deposit.percent.unit: % of the search and copying costs (full advance payment may be required); no partial-deposit cap in statute
rules.deposit.percent.notes: APRA has no deposit-percentage concept; the permission runs to the full copying/search cost. City may choose a smaller deposit as local policy.

payment.productionGate.label: Production may be conditioned on payment (pay before copies / pay in full before release)
payment.productionGate.value: copies: agency may require payment of search and copying costs in advance (pay-before-copies gate permitted) | inspection: never conditioned on any fee | e-mailed electronic copies: no fee at all | law-enforcement recording copies: advance payment of the ≤$150 copy fee upheld (25-FC-121)
payment.productionGate.notes: Gate is discretionary (may), not mandatory. Also § 8(f): agency 'shall collect' any fee specified by statute or ordered by a court (IN-9009).

payment.nonpayment.label: Nonpayment consequence (withdrawn after N days; prior-debt prepayment)
payment.nonpayment.notes: No deemed-withdrawal period, no prior-debt prepayment rule; the only statutory lever is advance payment (§ 8(e)). § 5-14-3-9's denial-timing rules (24 hours in person; 7 days for mail/fax requests) do not address nonpayment. rules.minFee.authority: Ind. Code § 5-14-3-8(d); PAC Op. 19-FC-67; cf. § 8(m) (schools: no minimum search fee)
rules.minFee.notes: No minimum-fee provision for municipalities; but a flat per-report fee that exceeds the per-page ceiling is unlawful (PAC 19-FC-67: $8 flat police-report fee 'not justifiable'), so any minimum must fit under $0.10/$0.25 × pages or actual cost. media.label: Electronic media (CD/DVD/USB) charge
media.value: 'direct cost of supplying the information in that form' — statutorily defined as 105% of (program development, if any) + (labor required to retrieve electronically stored data) + (medium used for electronic output); alternatively the standard price of a published version; law-enforcement recording copies capped at $150

Prior status pointed at IN-0012 (reprogramming) and IN-0017 (electronic map) — neither is the CD/DVD/USB rul…

delivery.label: Delivery: mail / handling / email / pickup
delivery.value: e-mail delivery of electronic copies: no fee (statute) | postal delivery: postage may be recouped as an actual cost per PAC guidance (19-FC-67 'postage costs to remote requesters'; 25-FC-326 'copying and postage') | in-person pickup: copy fee only | facsimile: 'facsimile machine transmission' fee only where specified by statute or court order (§ 8(f)); (d) 'actual cost' includes per-page cost of facsimile equipment
delivery.notes: E-mail no-fee rule is a Prohibition binding all public agencies. No statutory handling/mailing rate.

certification.label: Certification / certified-copy charge

av.label: Audio/video: per recording, per minute, free minutes
av.unit: USD per copy of a law enforcement recording (body-worn/vehicle camera); other audio/video duplicates: direct cost (105% of retrieval labor + medium); no per-minute rate; no free minutes
av.authority: Ind. Code § 5-14-3-8(g)(1); § 5-14-3-2 ('direct cost', 'law enforcement recording'); PAC Ops. 21-FC-131, 25-FC-121, 25-FC-152, 25-FC-221

An agency may only recoup its direct cost up to $150'); PAC has upheld local ordinances setting $150 where direct cost exceeds it (25-FC-121 Tippecanoe Co. commercial.label: Commercial-purpose schedule (surcharge %, labor becomes chargeable)
commercial.value: no commercial surcharge and no labor-becomes-chargeable rule; instead (i) a political subdivision MAY by ordinance prescribe conditions on commercial use of data received on disk/tape and bar violators from further data (§ 3(e)); (ii) electronic-map maintenance fee MAY be waived for noncommercial use (§ 8(k)); (iii) HEA 1360 (eff. 7/1/2026): agencies MAY prioritize Indiana residents and civic/journalistic/academic/personal-use requests and MAY charge non-Indiana/out-of-state requesters a supplemental fee ≤ $0.25/page + $25/hr (§§ 8.1, 8(n)); (iv) no purpose statement may be demanded as a condition of access (§ 3(a)), though a purpose is needed to receive § 8.1 priority
commercial.notes: The fee-bearing distinction Indiana draws is residency (in-state vs out-of-state) rather than commercial purpose. Lists of names/addresses may not be disclosed to commercial entities for commercial purposes (§ 3(f)) — a disclosure rule, not a fee.

waiver.label: Fee waiver: grounds, mandatory vs discretionary, purpose statement, written denial, appeal
waiver.value: no general fee-waiver provision (no indigence/public-interest waiver of copy fees; § 8(d) requires the local schedule to be 'uniform to all purchasers'); discretionary waivers exist only for: § 8(o) supplemental non-resident fee 'if the public agency finds that the public records request serves the public interest' (eff. 7/1/2026); § 8(k) electronic-map maintenance fee for noncommercial use; § 8(i) governmental-entity electronic-device inspection fee; no purpose statement may be required for access (§ 3(a)); no written-denial or appeal procedure for waiver decisions (PAC formal complaint is the general remedy)
waiver.notes: Waivers are Permissions (may), never mandatory. Categorical zero-fee items (inspection; e-mailed electronic copies) are prohibitions, not waivers.

waiver.forfeiture.label: Late response forfeits the fee
waiver.forfeiture.notes: No provision forfeits fees for a late response; APRA's remedies for untimely response are the deemed-denial triggers (§ 9(b)-(c)), PAC complaint, court action, and civil penalties (§ 9.5) — none touches fees. repeat.label: Repeat / aggregated requests (carry-forward, aggregation threshold)
repeat.notes: No fee aggregation threshold or carry-forward rule for repeat requests. HEA 1360 (2026) lets agencies delay/deprioritize requests 'identified as originating from out-of-state entities or automated systems' and decline suspected data-scraping/phishing requests (§ 3.3(b)) — routing/priority rules, …

fee.copy_rate_per_page.summary: The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of ten cents ($0.10) per non-color page or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per color page, or the agency's actual cost.

fee.electronic_media_charge.summary: An agency may charge the requester the agency's direct cost of reprogramming a computer system where reprogramming is required to separate disclosable from nondisclosable information stored electronically.
An agency may charge a fee for providing an electronic map based upon a reasonable percentage of the agency's direct cost of maintaining, upgrading, and enhancing the electronic map.

fee.certified_copy_charge.summary: The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document.

fee.special_service_charge.summary: An agency may charge any reasonable fee agreed on in an enhanced-access contract under section 3.5 for providing enhanced access to public records.

fee.schedule_and_authority.summary: For a local public agency, the fiscal body of the political subdivision establishes the copying fee schedule by ordinance, and the fee must be uniform.
For a local public agency, the fiscal body of the political subdivision establishes the copying fee schedule by ordinance, and the fee must be uniform.
